- Diversification: REITs allow investors to expand their portfolios, adding real estate assets without committing a large sum upfront.

# Tarout Castle: A Visit-Worthy Treasure Among Dammam Tourist Places

This 5,000-year-old fortress lies quietly on Tarout Island in the Al-Qatif region, almost as if it’s waiting to be rediscovered. Just a short trip from Dammam, Tarout Castle stands as a reminder of an ancient world that’s rarely glimpsed in the region’s more popular Marina Mall . ## Quick Facts About Tarout Castle

- Location: Tarout Island, Al-Qatif region, Eastern Saudi Arabia
- Distance from Dammam: Approximately 50 kilometers
- Age: Estimated to be over 5,000 years old, making it one of the oldest historic sites in the area
- Architecture: Constructed primarily from limestone and coral, with ancient fortification features

Tarout Castle has seen millennia of life, from ancient traders of Mesopotamia to explorers of the Arabian Peninsula. It’s a place where time almost stands still—a fortress built to withstand centuries and tell the stories of those who’ve come and gone. The rugged beauty of its limestone walls and the simplicity of its structure give it a haunting yet captivating allure.  The limestone walls of Tarout Castle are timeless. They are layered with remnants of the past, from faint engravings to the natural wear from centuries of exposure. Walking through them feels like stepping back into a world vastly different from ours, defined by a deep connection to history.
2. Elevated Views of Tarout Island
 The castle’s elevated position on the island offers incredible views across the sea and the surrounding groves. The landscape is peaceful, almost serene, giving you the perfect vantage point to imagine ancient sailors and traders as they approached the island. Today, the view remains unobstructed, allowing you to experience a slice of this ancient world.
3. Archaeological Significance
 Tarout Castle is more than a historic site; it’s a time capsule. Archaeologists have unearthed pottery, weapons, and inscriptions that tie the island to ancient civilizations, including Mesopotamia. This archaeological significance makes it one of the most fascinating things to do in Dammam for history lovers and curious travelers alike.

# The Majesty of King Fahd Fountain: A Stunning Jeddah Marvel

When you think of Jeddah, one of the first things that may come to mind is the beautiful King Fahd Fountain. Towering majestically over the Red Sea, it’s not just the tallest fountain in the world but also a symbol of the city’s resilience, spirit, and connection to water. For many who visit or live in Jeddah, the fountain offers an iconic reminder of the city’s beauty. Whether strolling down the Jeddah Corniche or watching the sunset, the King Fahd Fountain is impossible to miss.

But there’s so much more to this incredible feature of Jeddah beyond its height and grandeur. In this piece, we’ll explore everything you need to know about the fountain in Jeddah—from its history to how it can enhance your visit.

## The Historical Legacy of the King Fahd Fountain

The King Fahd Fountain—sometimes simply referred to as the Jeddah Fountain—was a gift from King Fahd bin Abdulaziz to the city of Jeddah. It was designed as a symbol of beauty and a reflection of Jeddah’s vibrant culture and strategic location on the Red Sea.

- Completion Year: 1985
- Location: Nestled on the western coast of Saudi Arabia along the Jeddah Corniche, the fountain stands a great tourist attraction.

The fountain is even more incredible because it uses saltwater drawn directly from the Red Sea, unlike other fountains worldwide that often rely on freshwater systems. The salty waters of the Red Sea are pumped to remarkable heights, showing the ingenuity of its design and the unique challenges it overcomes.

## King Fahd Fountain: The World’s Tallest Fountain

So, how high is the King Fahd Fountain? At an astounding 312 meters (1,024 feet), this Jeddah fountain’s height makes it the tallest in the world. For comparison, that’s taller than the Eiffel Tower without its antenna! When you stand at the base of the Corniche and look up, it’s impossible not to feel a sense of awe at the sheer magnitude of this engineering marvel.

- Water Velocity: The fountain pumps water at 375 km/h (233 mph).
- Water Volume: About 625 liters (165 gallons) of water are pushed into the air each second.

Imagine standing there, feeling the cool mist on your skin as the water droplets cascade back down, the rushing water roaring in the background—an experience that moves you.

## The Best Time to Visit King Fahd Fountain in Jeddah

The King Fahd Fountain in Jeddah is a must-see attraction at any time of the year. But for those who wish to make the most of their experience, the best time to visit is sunset or the early evening. At night, the fountain is illuminated by hundreds of lights, making the spectacle even more magical as it reflects off the calm waters of the Red Sea. The contrast of light against the inky black sky is mesmerizing.

Walking along the Jeddah Corniche fountain during these hours offers a peaceful and romantic atmosphere for families, couples, and solo travelers alike.

If you’re visiting Jeddah briefly, there are other attractions nearby that you can pair with your visit to the fountain. Check out Tahlia Street Jeddah for shopping and dining experiences after a beautiful evening by the water.

## Why the King Fahd Fountain is Important to Jeddah

The fountain in Jeddah isn’t just a beautiful sight—it’s an integral part of the city’s identity. For locals, it symbolizes home, culture, and pride. It draws people to the Jeddah Corniche, promoting the community as they gather with their loved ones to admire its beauty.

Furthermore, the King Fahd Fountain plays a crucial role in driving tourism. People from all over the world come to witness the stunning height and beauty of the fountain. If the allure of the Jeddah fountain has captured your heart and you’re considering staying in the area, you’ll find various housing options to suit every need and budget. You can also read more about apartments for rent in Jeddah for expats .

Whether you’re planning a short-term stay or looking to settle in Jeddah long-term, the city offers different rental options to accommodate different lifestyles. And with the King Fahd Fountain nearby, your evenings can be spent admiring the world’s tallest fountain—a sight you’ll never tire of.

In conclusion, the King Fahd Fountain is an attraction and an experience. It’s a must-visit for anyone in Jeddah, offering beauty and serenity. Let the height of the Jeddah fountain inspire you as you explore this remarkable city’s culture, history, and hospitality.

The King Fahd Fountain is the tallest in the world, standing at 312 meters. Its use of salt water from the Red Sea sets it apart from other significant fountains around the globe, and its strategic location on the Jeddah Corniche enhances its visibility and grandeur.

The fountain is visible year-round, but the best time to visit is at sunset or in the evening when the lights come on. The lights create a mesmerizing visual experience against the backdrop of the Red Sea.

The fountain can be seen from various parts of the city, especially from the Jeddah Corniche. Its towering height makes it visible from miles away, providing a stunning focal point from numerous vantage points.

Yes! Visitors can enjoy nearby attractions such as Tahlia Street , Aziz Mall Jeddah , and Jeddah International Exhibition & Convention Center . There are also beautiful parks and beaches along the Corniche where you can relax after viewing the fountain.

## A Miracle in Makkah: The Birth of Zamzam Well

Zamzam Well is located in Makkah, just a few meters east of the Kaaba, Islam’s most sacred site. The well has been a vital source of water for over 4,000 years, and it all started with divine intervention.

Legend has it that Hajar (Hagar), the wife of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham), was left alone with her infant son, Ismail, in the desert of Makkah. Desperate for water, Hajar ran between the hills of Safa and Marwah for sustenance. After her seventh run, Angel Jibril (Gabriel) appeared and struck the ground with his wing. In that instant, water gushed forth, and thus, Zamzam Well was born. Zamzam Makkah is more than a well; it symbolizes faith and perseverance that every Muslim holds dear.

## The Unmatched Purity of Zamzam Well Water

Zamzam water is no ordinary water. It’s said to have healing properties, and Muslims believe Allah has blessed it. The water has been analyzed multiple times over the years and has consistently proven to be one of the purest forms of water on earth, free from impurities and rich in essential minerals.

### Here’s what makes Zamzam Well so unique:

- Mineral Richness: Zamzam water contains higher levels of calcium and magnesium than other types of water, which contributes to its reputation for healing properties.
- No Biological Contamination: Despite being an open well, Zamzam Water has never shown any signs of biological contamination.
- Constant Flow: The well has never run dry despite millions of pilgrims drawing water from it yearly.

It’s not just pilgrims who seek out this blessed water; people worldwide crave its purity and holiness. You might be searching for “Zamzam water near me” right now. Many countries have limited imports of Zamzam water, making it a rare and highly valued gift among Muslims.

## The Spiritual Significance of Zamzam in Islamic Rituals

Zamzam is an integral part of the Islamic pilgrimage known as Hajj and Umrah. Pilgrims perform the ritual of drinking Zamzam water while they are in Makkah, and it is highly encouraged to drink from the well after completing Tawaf, the act of circling the Kaaba.

### Essential spiritual practices involving Zamzam water:

- Dua while drinking: Muslims often make a personal prayer or “dua” while drinking Zamzam, as it’s believed that prayers made at this moment are answered.
- Bringing water back home: Pilgrims often bring back bottles of Zamzam water to share with family and friends, extending the blessings of the holy city beyond Makkah.

Pilgrims also use Zamzam water for purification and cleansing, reinforcing its role in Islamic life and worship.

## A Modern Marvel: The Engineering Behind the Well

It’s fascinating how something so ancient still functions seamlessly in the modern world. Zamzam Well has been engineered to withstand the needs of millions of pilgrims annually. Modern pumps and pipes ensure the water can be easily accessed and distributed throughout Makkah and beyond.

### Here’s a breakdown of the well’s structure:

- Depth: Zamzam well is approximately 30 meters deep, ensuring a continuous fresh water supply.
- Flow rate: It’s estimated that Zamzam water is replenished at a rate of 11-18 liters per second, enough to meet the demand of thousands of pilgrims.
- Advanced Technology: Today, the Zamzam water system utilizes advanced purification technology to ensure pilgrims can always access clean, pure water.

This combination of ancient miracles and modern engineering makes Zamzam Well one of the world’s most unique resources.

After learning about the holiness of Zamzam water, you might be wondering where you can get some. During Hajj or Umrah, it’s common for pilgrims to take bottles of Zamzam water home. You can also find Zamzam water in various Islamic shops and mosques worldwide.

Zamzam is more than a well or a source of water. It’s deeply woven into Islamic culture and is significant in daily life, rituals, and even folklore. It’s common for Muslims to gift Zamzam water during special occasions such as weddings or after returning from Hajj or Umrah.

Whether sipping on it during Hajj or bringing it home for loved ones, Zamzam water will always remind you of the miracles and faith that define the Islamic world.

# Nassif House Museum: An Amazing Historic Treasure in the Heart of Jeddah

Welcome to Jeddah, the dazzling port city on the Red Sea that seamlessly blends ancient history with modern living. Whether you’re a history buff, an art lover, or simply curious about the city’s rich culture, a trip to Nassif House Museum is a must! Nestled in the heart of Al Balad, Jeddah’s historic district, this museum isn’t just a building—it’s a storyteller of Jeddah’s past, a witness to its development, and a treasure chest of Islamic and regional art.

In this blog, we’ll explore everything you need to know about Nassif House Museum and why it should be on your must-visit list when exploring museums in Jeddah.

## What Is Nassif House Museum?

Let’s start with the basics. Nassif House Museum, also known as Nassif House Jeddah, is a cultural beacon in Al Balad, Jeddah. Originally a family home built in the late 19th century, this architectural marvel was converted into a museum and cultural center. The museum has long been associated with prominent historical figures and even served as a venue for formal events in the city’s political and social history.

### A Bit of History

- Construction: Nassif House was constructed in the late 1800s by Sheikh Omar Effendi Nassif, an influential merchant and governor of Jeddah.
- Historical Significance: The house played a significant role in the Kingdom’s history, as King Abdulaziz Ibn Saud, the founder of modern Saudi Arabia, stayed here during his visits to Jeddah.
- Architectural Design: The house’s design is a beautiful blend of Islamic architecture and traditional Hejazi craftsmanship. Its towering structure, intricate wooden latticework, and large wooden doors are true testaments to the architectural beauty of old Jeddah.

## Why Nassif House Museum Is a Must-Visit?

If you’re interested in experiencing Islamic art museums in Jeddah or in Jeddah in general, Nassif House Museum offers a comprehensive cultural experience you won’t find elsewhere.

- Architectural Marvel: You’ll be awestruck by its classic design, which features elements like wooden Roshan windows, carved doors, and spacious courtyards that create a sense of grandeur.
- Historical Exhibits: The museum boasts a rich collection of artifacts, photos, and exhibits illustrating Jeddah’s evolution from a trading post to a modern city.
- Islamic Art and Culture: The museum offers unique insights into Islamic art, including calligraphy, textiles, and ceramics, which reflect Jeddah’s diverse cultural history.
- Cultural Heritage: As one of the oldest buildings in Jeddah, Nassif House showcases the city’s deep roots and importance as a gateway for pilgrims traveling to Mecca.

## What You’ll See Inside Nassif House Museum

Let’s talk specifics. You’re stepping back in time when you step inside Nassif House Jeddah. Each floor of the museum tells a unique story worth listening to, offering a rich blend of exhibits and artifacts:

- Ground Floor: The entrance opens to a spacious courtyard where visitors can admire traditional Islamic architecture up close. There, they can also find a collection of old photographs and documents that highlight Jeddah’s past.
- Upper Floors: The upper floors are filled with Islamic art, traditional Hejazi furniture, and collections that reflect the daily life of Jeddah’s elite in the 19th and early 20th centuries.

# The National Museum in Riyadh: Explore Saudi Arabia’s Interesting History

The National Museum in Riyadh isn’t just a building entire of artifacts; it reflects Saudi Arabia’s rich culture, history, and deep connection to the past. Nestled in the heart of the capital, it invites visitors to step into a world where ancient civilizations come to life, the deserts breathe stories, and the modern history of the Kingdom is seamlessly integrated with its historical roots. The National Museum is an essential stop on your itinerary if you’re visiting Riyadh.

## An Overview of the National History Museum

The National Museum in Riyadh, located within the King Abdulaziz Historical Center, offers visitors a comprehensive look into the historical and cultural development of the Arabian Peninsula. Visitors explore the early stages of human civilization, the Islamic era, and the formation of modern-day Saudi Arabia through carefully curated exhibits. It’s more than just a typical national history museum—it provides a thoughtful perspective on how history shapes the present.

### The Structure and Layout

The museum’s architecture is as fascinating as the exhibits themselves. It’s modern but draws inspiration from traditional Arabian design, a perfect blend of old and new. Inside, the museum is divided into eight distinct sections or galleries, each telling a unique part of Saudi Arabia’s story:

- Man and Universe Gallery: This section takes you through the geological history of the Arabian Peninsula.
- Arabian Kingdoms Gallery: A deep dive into the pre-Islamic period of the Arabian Peninsula, filled with stories of ancient kingdoms.
- Islam and the Arabian Peninsula Gallery: This gallery focuses on the advent of Islam and highlights the region’s rapid transformation.
- First and Second Saudi States Gallery: Detailing the rise of the Saudi states and their impact on the Arabian Peninsula.
- Unification Gallery: It covers the monumental moments in the establishment of modern Saudi Arabia.
- Hajj and the Two Holy Mosques Gallery: A beautiful exhibition of the importance of Hajj in Islamic culture.
- Saudi Arabia Today Gallery: This section emphasizes the rapid development of the Kingdom.

Walking through these galleries gives you a sense of not only history but also how Saudi Arabia views itself in the modern world.

## The Importance of Visiting the National Museum

Why should you visit the National Museum in Riyadh? There’s something about seeing history before your eyes that deepens your understanding of a place, especially one as layered as Saudi Arabia. Here are a few compelling reasons:

- Cultural Immersion: Whether a local or a tourist, stepping into the Riyadh Museum gives you a glimpse of a shared history and a communal sense of identity.
- Educational Experience: The museum’s exhibits are well-researched and deeply informative. It’s perfect for students, history buffs, or anyone curious about the past.
- Modern Meets Ancient: Combining modern technology with ancient relics creates an engaging experience. Visitors are not just looking at static objects—they are engaging with interactive displays, films, and models that bring history to life.

## Riyadh Museum Entrance Fee

One of the visitors’ most frequently asked questions is about the National Museum Riyadh entrance fee. The entrance fee is quite affordable, making it accessible to locals and tourists. Here’s a breakdown:

- Adults: Around SAR 10
- Children and Students: Free entry
- Groups: Special discounts are available for groups.

The affordable fee encourages everyone to experience the museum’s cultural richness without financial barriers. For tourists exploring tourism in Saudi Arabia , this is a must-see destination.

National Museum in Riyadh is open every day except Fridays, and operating hours are generally from 9 a.m. to 8 p.m. However, checking for updated opening times is always wise, especially during national holidays or special events.

It is recommended that you visit on weekdays, especially in the morning, to avoid crowds. That way, you can have more time to explore at your own pace without the rush.

## The Enigmatic Wadi E Jinn History

Wadi E Jinn has captivated the imaginations of locals and visitors for centuries. This valley, located about 30 kilometers northwest of Madinah, has long been a subject of mystery. The region’s name, “Wadi Al Jinn” (or Wadi E Jin), suggests a connection to the ancient tales of Jinn, supernatural beings mentioned in Islamic tradition.

### The Legends of Wadi E Jin

In Arabic folklore, Jinn are powerful creatures made from smokeless fire. They are often seen as tricksters or beings with immense power, capable of influencing the natural world in ways humans cannot comprehend. Many locals believe that Wadi E Jin is home to these spirits, so vehicles seem to defy gravity when moving independently.

## The Science Behind the Mystery

While many visitors are eager to embrace the supernatural explanation for Wadi E Jin’s mysterious occurrences, scientists have provided an alternative theory. The “mystery” of cars moving uphill may be an optical illusion called “gravity hill.”

### What is a Gravity Hill?

Gravity hills are places where the surrounding landscape creates the illusion that a slight downhill slope is uphill. This visual trickery happens because the horizon and surrounding terrain distort our perception of what is genuinely flat or inclined.

- Optical Illusion: The terrain around Wadi Jinn Madinah makes it look like cars are moving uphill when, in reality, they are going downhill.

# Exploring The Amazing Clock Tower Museum: A Journey Through Time in Makkah

The Clock Tower Makkah Museum is a hidden gem nestled within one of Makkah’s most iconic landmarks—the Clock Tower, part of the expansive Makkah Clock Tower Hotel complex. This marvel of architecture and history offers visitors an immersive experience that blends the past, present, and future. Whether you are an avid traveler or a first-time visitor, the museum provides a deep dive into the rich history of Islamic timekeeping, astronomy, and the technological advancements behind the famous clock.

In this article, we will explain everything you need to know about the Clock Tower Museum, its historical significance, and why it stands out among Makkah tourist attractions . We cover everything from the Makkah Tower Hotel to the museum’s interactive exhibits.

## Overview of the Clock Tower Museum

The Clock Tower Museum is located in the heart of Makkah. It occupies the uppermost floors of the Clock Tower, part of the Abraj Al Bait Complex. The museum is divided into four distinct levels, each providing an insightful exploration of various aspects of timekeeping, the lunar calendar, and the role of astronomy in Islam.

### Key Features:

- Floor 1: The Universe – Visitors are introduced to the astronomical wonders of the universe, with detailed exhibits on stars, planets, and galaxies.
- Floor 2: The Solar System – A closer look at our solar system, its mechanics, and how it relates to Islamic timekeeping, such as prayer times.
- Floor 3: The Sun and Moon – An exploration of how Islamic scholars have used the positions of the sun and moon to determine important dates and times in the Islamic calendar.
- Floor 4: The Makkah Clock—This is the pinnacle of the museum, featuring the inner workings of the world’s largest clock face. Here, visitors can marvel at the intricate mechanics and engineering behind the Makkah Clock Tower, an icon of faith and innovation.

### Why Visit the Clock Tower Museum?

- Educational Insight: The museum offers a unique perspective on Islamic timekeeping and astronomy, deeply intertwined with the history of the Islamic world.
- Unrivaled Views: The museum is situated in Makkah’s tallest tower, providing panoramic views of the Holy Kaaba and the surrounding city. It’s an experience like no other.
- Cultural Importance: The museum reminds visitors of the importance of time in Islamic culture, especially the significance of lunar cycles in determining religious observances like Ramadan and Eid.

## Clock Tower: A Symbol of Modern Makkah

The Clock Tower is one of the world’s most recognizable structures. More than just an attraction, it is a symbol of Makkah’s modernization and progress. As part of the Makkah Tower Hotel complex, the tower is also a functional aspect of daily life for pilgrims and visitors to the city. The clock is the biggest in the world, visible from up to 25 kilometers.

### Fun Facts About the Makkah Clock Tower:

- Size: The clock’s face is a staggering 43 meters in diameter.
- Height: The Clock Tower is part of the more prominent Makkah Clock Tower Hotel, which stands at 601 meters tall, making it the third tallest building in the world.
- Call to Prayer: The clock emits a beautiful call to prayer, amplified by 21,000 green and white lights, visible even from distant points of Makkah.

## The Makkah Tower Hotel: Luxury Meets Spirituality

For those seeking accommodation in Makkah, the Makkah Clock Tower Hotel offers one of the best locations in the city. It’s luxurious and provides a direct view of the Masjid Al Haram and the Holy Kaaba. ### Top Reasons to Stay at the Makkah Tower Hotel:

- Proximity to the Haram: You are just steps away from the Masjid Al Haram, ensuring you never miss a prayer or moment of reflection.
- World-Class Amenities: The Makkah Clock Tower Hotel offers unparalleled hospitality, from luxurious suites to exquisite dining options.

Jeddah is a city that thrives on its vibrant blend of culture, history, and modernity. On its famous Corniche lies a world that offers more than just a thrill—Al Shallal Theme Park in Jeddah is an oasis of entertainment, family fun, and adrenaline-pumping rides. Here’s everything you need to know about this fascinating destination—where the rides aren’t just rides. They are stories etched into the soul of Jeddah.

Visiting Al Shallal Amusement Park isn’t just about having fun—it’s also about making sure your trip is hassle-free. The ticket prices are affordable and designed to give you the best experience without burning a hole in your pocket.

Al Shallal Theme Park is conveniently located along the Jeddah Corniche, making it easily accessible for locals and tourists. Its strategic location lets visitors enjoy the theme park and explore the surrounding area, which is rich with cultural and modern attractions.

Jeddah’s climate can be hot, but evenings at Al Shallal Park are excellent, thanks to its seaside location. The best time to visit is during the cooler months between October and March, when temperatures are milder, and the park remains open late into the night.

Al Shallal Theme Park is open from 5:00 PM to 1:00 AM during weekdays and from 5:00 PM till 2:00 AM on weekends. However, it’s best to check the official website for updates, as timings may vary on special occasions or during festivals.

While there isn’t an official dress code, modest and comfortable attire is recommended, especially since you’ll be walking and participating in various rides. Swimwear is required for certain water rides, so don’t forget to pack accordingly.

Yes, you can purchase Al Shallal theme park tickets online, which is highly recommended to avoid long queues, especially on weekends and holidays.

Yes, Al Shallal Park Jeddah offers discounts for large groups, schools, and corporate outings. For more details, it’s best to contact their customer service in advance.

# King Fahad Park Dammam: A Beautiful Green Oasis in Saudi Arabia’s Bustling Eastern Province

Dammam, a city known for its modern infrastructure and vibrant urban life, offers residents and visitors a balance of tranquility amidst the cityscape. Among the gems in the city is King Fahad Park, a sprawling oasis of greenery, water features, and family-friendly attractions. For those seeking a respite from the bustle of life in the Eastern Province, this park delivers an unparalleled experience. In this guide, we’ll explore the historical significance, attractions, and proximity to critical landmarks like King Fahd Hospital and Dammam Corniche while delving into why this park stands out among other parks in Dammam.

## A Historical Glimpse: The Vision Behind King Fahad Park

King Fahad Park, named after the legendary Saudi monarch King Fahd, is not just another recreational area—it symbolizes the kingdom’s dedication to urban beautification and the well-being of its citizens. Opened in the 1980s, this park was envisioned as a place where families, tourists, and residents could relax amidst nature, far from the crowded urban zones. It spans over 1,120 acres, making it the largest park in Dammam and one of the biggest in the entire Gulf region.

Key Features of King Fahad Park:

- Vast Greenery: With carefully landscaped lawns, tall palm trees, and wide-open spaces, the park offers serenity in every corner. It’s a place where children can run freely while adults find relaxing spots.
- Water Features: Numerous fountains and artificial lakes are dotted around the park, adding to its tranquil charm.
- Entertainment Zones: The park houses several amusement rides for families, offering activities that cater to people of all ages.
- Sport Facilities: There are jogging tracks, cycling paths, and spaces for team sports like soccer and volleyball.

## King Fahad Park Dammam: The Heart of Leisure in the Eastern Province

King Fahad Park Dammam stands out not only due to its sheer size but also because of its proximity to vital urban centers like King Fahd Hospital. Whether planning a stroll or a family picnic, this park is a hub of relaxation and recreational activities. With its central location, it’s easily accessible for both locals and tourists, making it an ideal destination for weekend outings or even weekday breaks.

King Fahad Park is close to some of Dammam’s most significant landmarks. It’s a stone’s throw from the King Fahd Hospital, making it ideal for patients and visitors seeking a natural escape. Moreover, its proximity to Al Hayat Plaza Dammam and other major shopping centers makes it a perfect blend of nature and urban convenience.

Why King Fahad Park is a Must-Visit:

- Accessibility: Its central location makes it accessible to everyone, whether coming from King Fahd Hospital, Almana General Hospital Dammam, or nearby residential areas.
- Family-Friendly: With expansive play areas, picnic spots, and walking trails, it’s a top spot for families.
- Cultural Significance: The park is often a site for community events and celebrations, reflecting the city’s cultural fabric.

## The Role of Parks in Dammam’s Urban Landscape

In a city like Dammam, where rapid urbanization and economic growth are constant, parks like King Fahad Park are more than just recreational spaces. They are the city’s lungs. Green spaces are crucial for maintaining the environmental balance in urban areas, providing residents with spaces to breathe, relax, and recharge.

### Other Noteworthy Parks in Dammam:

## The Story of UBT: Building a Legacy in Jeddah

Jeddah is more than just a beautiful coastal city on the Red Sea; it’s also a thriving educational hub. The University of Business & Technology Jeddah (UBT) was established in 2000, first as a specialized institute focusing on business education, which quickly expanded to offer diverse undergraduate and postgraduate programs. Today, it’s one of the most prestigious universities in the region.

UBT has two primary campuses—one in Dhahban, with sprawling green landscapes that provide a peaceful environment for learning, and the other in Sari, which is more compact and city-centric. UBT’s commitment to education is evident in its focus on business, engineering, and law programs. This university in Jeddah has come a long way since its early days, with accreditation from prestigious global bodies and partnerships with prominent institutions like Arab Open University and King Saud University .

### The Vision and Mission of UBT

Let’s be honest here. Universities are great, but sometimes they can feel a bit…out of touch with what students need. That’s where UBT Jeddah comes in. Their mission is to bridge the gap between academia and the demands of the professional world. They’ve aligned their educational goals with Vision 2030, which aims to prepare students for the future job market while contributing to Saudi Arabia’s growth and development.

This means many of the programs at UBT are industry-focused, with practical applications that ensure graduates aren’t just sitting around with diplomas—they’re prepared to tackle the world. With partnerships in the business, tech, and industrial sectors, it’s a place where education meets innovation.

This diversity means you can explore different career paths while enjoying the flexibility of various courses.

### 4. Accreditation

## UBT Jeddah Fees: What You Need to Know

Of course, we can’t discuss the University of Business and Technology Jeddah without discussing the cost. UBT Jeddah fees are competitive for the region, but it’s essential to understand the breakdown before deciding.

- Undergraduate Programs: The fees for undergraduate programs like business, law, or engineering typically range between SAR 50,000 and SAR 60,000 per academic year. However, this can vary based on specific courses and materials.
- Postgraduate Programs: UBT’s MBA program is one of the most sought-after in Jeddah, and the fees reflect the value you get in return. Expect to pay around SAR 90,000 for the entire program, though this might change based on specializations.
- Scholarships: The good news? UBT Jeddah offers a range of scholarships and financial aid options. You may qualify for tuition reductions or grants if you’re an outstanding student.

It’s essential to weigh these costs against the quality of education you’ll receive and the career opportunities post-graduation. After all, investing in a high-quality education can pay off in the long run.

We’ve talked a lot about academics, but what about campus life? UBT Jeddah boasts a vibrant student life, offering much more than just classes.

### 1. Extracurriculars and Clubs

- UBT encourages students to participate in extracurricular activities that range from cultural and artistic clubs to sports teams. Whether you’re into debating, entrepreneurship, or basketball, there’s something for everyone.

### 2. Facilities

- Both campuses have state-of-the-art facilities, including modern classrooms, libraries, and labs. The Dhahban campus, in particular, is known for its scenic views and green spaces, which make it one of the most attractive university campuses in Jeddah.

Here’s the thing about UBT graduates—they’re well-prepared for the job market. With strong links to the business community, a UBT degree doesn’t just sit in a frame gathering dust. Graduates often find positions in industries like finance, law, and engineering. The University of Business and Technology Jeddah has a Career Development Center that works closely with companies to ensure their students land great jobs.

### Internships and Job Placement

- One of the standout features of UBT Jeddah is its emphasis on internships. Most students complete internships during their degree, which helps them build professional networks and gain work experience. By the time graduation rolls around, they’re already ahead of the competition.

## Comparing UBT Jeddah with Other Universities in Jeddah

UBT Jeddah stands out in the crowded field of higher education in Jeddah, but how does it compare to other universities? For instance, King Saud University is one of the oldest and most established universities in Saudi Arabia, while Abdulaziz University Jeddah is known for its extensive research programs.

Ultimately, your choice between these universities depends on your career goals, field of interest, and how you want your university experience to develop.

## Exploring Jeddah: Living the Student Life

Jeddah is a vibrant city with much to offer. Whether you’re moving here for the first time or you’ve been a lifelong resident, student life in Jeddah provides a unique blend of culture, history, and modern amenities. There’s always something to do, from exploring historical sites to hanging out at the waterfront. Plus, if you’re looking for more permanent housing, properties for sale in Ar Riyadh provide excellent long-term options for families and professionals.

In summary, UBT Jeddah is more than just a university in Jeddah—it’s a stepping stone to a promising future, offering quality education, industry connections, and global opportunities. Whether you’re looking for academic excellence, practical experience, or a blend of both, the University of Business and Technology Jeddah might be your perfect match.

UBT Jeddah provides scholarships based on merit and financial need, ensuring deserving students can afford a world-class education.

The student-to-faculty ratio at UBT is designed to provide personalized education with smaller class sizes than more prominent public universities.

UBT Jeddah holds international accreditations for several of its programs, making its degrees recognized globally, which is particularly beneficial for students aiming to work abroad.

# Saudi National Day 2025: An Amazing Celebration of Culture, Unity, and Progress

Saudi National Day, celebrated annually on September 23rd, is the foundation of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in 1932 by King Abdulaziz Al Saud. It’s more than just a national holiday; it reflects Saudi Arabia’s unity, heritage, and continuous journey towards growth and development. As the country steps into the global spotlight, particularly with significant events like the upcoming Expo 2030 and aspirations for hosting the World Cup in Saudi Arabia , Saudi National Day symbolizes the Kingdom’s past and promising future.

## The Meaning Behind Saudi National Day

Every year, the streets of the Kingdom are adorned with green flags, the national colors of Saudi Arabia, and the air fills with a sense of pride and unity. But what makes this national holiday so significant?

The history of Saudi Celebration National Day dates back to when King Abdulaziz declared the unification of the disparate regions of Nejd and Hejaz into a single nation-state, now known as the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA). This unification created a robust and cohesive country and laid the foundation for its modernization and strategic importance on the global stage.

As citizens celebrate KSA National Day, they remember the sacrifices made by their ancestors and take pride in the country’s rich Islamic heritage. Various cultural events, parades, and fireworks across all major cities, including Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam, mark the day. It’s a time for citizens and expatriates to come together and celebrate the Kingdom’s progress.

## Saudi National Day 2025: A Glimpse into the Celebrations

The Saudi National Day 2025 was particularly significant as it reflected the Kingdom’s vision of transformation and modernization under the ambitious Saudi Vision 2030 initiative. The national holiday was celebrated with grandeur and patriotism, from concerts by leading Saudi artists to dazzling fireworks lit up the night sky. For anyone living in or visiting the Kingdom during this period, it was a testament to Saudi Arabia’s growing confidence and the increasingly vibrant lifestyle emerging across the nation.

In addition to the national celebrations, there was a particular emphasis on promoting tourism in Saudi Arabia . The government encouraged visitors and locals to explore the Kingdom’s rich historical sites and modern attractions. With the opening of new tourist destinations like Al-Ula and NEOM, Saudi National Day 2022 was an opportunity to showcase how the Kingdom positions itself as a key player in global tourism.

 - Traditional Dances and Music: The national holiday wouldn’t be complete without traditional performances like the “Ardah,” a sword dance performed by men wearing the national dress, accompanied by drums and chanting.

 - Historical Reenactments: Across various cities, reenactments of the events leading to Saudi Arabia’s founding are staged, providing citizens with a vivid portrayal of the country’s unification.

 - Concerts and Fireworks: National holidays in Saudi Arabia, especially Saudi National Day, are marked by large-scale concerts featuring local and international artists. The day usually culminates in fireworks displays lighting up the major cities.
 - Public Engagement: In recent years, there has been an increased push to engage citizens through social media campaigns, interactive events in malls, and augmented reality to connect people to the historical significance of the day.

## The Significance of Saudi Arabia National Day in Modern Times

Saudi National Day isn’t just a celebration of the past; it reflects where Saudi Arabia is heading. The country has seen rapid growth and development, from its thriving energy sector to its burgeoning real estate market, with properties for rent and even floors for sale increasingly sought after.

This day highlights the Kingdom’s ongoing transformation as part of Vision 2030, an initiative to diversify the Saudi economy from oil dependence. Additionally, Saudi Arabia’s social reforms, particularly those that give women more freedoms and allow entertainment industries to flourish, have made Saudi National Day a much more inclusive celebration. It reflects a nation opening its doors to the world and inviting others to share in its progress.

This is particularly relevant as more expatriates move to the Kingdom, drawn by the country’s growing opportunities and relatively low cost of living in Saudi Arabia .

Apart from Saudi National Day, there are other significant national holidays in the Kingdom, including Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha. However, Saudi National Day is a unique occasion that unites all citizens, regardless of background, to celebrate their shared heritage and the nation’s future ambitions.

With the Kingdom becoming increasingly accessible to foreign visitors and investors, national holidays like Saudi National Day serve as an essential bridge between the local population and the rest of the world.

In recent years, the Saudi Arabia Foundation Day celebration has gained prominence. While Saudi National Day focuses on the country’s unification in 1932, Foundation Day highlights the country’s deeper historical roots.

Both holidays complement each other, showcasing Saudi Arabia’s rich history while emphasizing its vision for the future. With Vision 2030 aiming to create a more sustainable and diversified economy, these national celebrations remind the Kingdom of its ongoing transformation.

As the world looks to Saudi Arabia for its role in global initiatives like Expo 2030 and possibly the World Cup in Saudi Arabia, the importance of Saudi National Day will only grow. It will serve as a reflection of the Kingdom’s accomplishments and its aspirations for the future.

# The Mystical Significance of Hira Makkah: A Journey to the Amazing Mount Hira

In the heart of the bustling city of Makkah lies a mountain steeped in spiritual significance and history, a place where the physical and the metaphysical meet. Hira Makkah, also known as Jabal al Nour, is important in Islamic tradition. On this mountain, in the small cave of Hira, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) received the initial revelation of the Holy Qur’an. A visit to Mount Hira is more than just a climb; it’s an immersion into the soul of Islamic history.

## Why Hira Makkah is Important

Hira Makkah, or Jabal al Nour, is one of the most revered sites for Muslims worldwide. It is a place where seekers of knowledge and peace can connect with the early days of Islam. At its peak sits Gare Hira Makkah, the cave where the Prophet Muhammad would often retreat for reflection and prayer. In 610 CE, it was here that the Angel Jibreel (Gabriel) first appeared to him with the divine message from Allah.

Visiting Hira Cave Makkah offers a profound sense of spirituality and connection to the origins of Islam. This place holds such a magnetic pull that millions of pilgrims from across the globe attempt the climb every year despite its difficulty.

## Climbing Jabal al Nour: A Pilgrim’s Challenge

Reaching Hira Cave Makkah isn’t an easy feat. The climb up Mount Hira can take 45 minutes to two hours, depending on your fitness level. The terrain is steep and rocky, but the reward is a stunning view of Makkah and, more importantly, a deep connection to Islamic history.

### Key Points to Know About Climbing Hira Mountain Makkah:

- Start Early: The best time to begin the climb is early morning before the sun gets too hot. Since Makkah’s temperatures can soar, the coolness of the early morning is ideal for such a physically demanding ascent.
- Proper Footwear: The path is rugged, so wearing sturdy hiking shoes is essential.
- Stay Hydrated: Bring plenty of water, as there are no facilities along the route.
- Take Breaks: Don’t rush. It’s a spiritual journey, so pause to reflect and appreciate the surroundings.

Once at the top, the serenity of Gare Hira Makkah is overwhelming. The cave itself is small and straightforward, but its significance is immeasurable. It’s a place that feels suspended between the physical world and the divine.

## Jabal al Nour History: The Beacon of Light

Jabal al Nour, meaning “Mountain of Light,” reflects its spiritual radiance. Although its history stretches back to pre-Islamic times, the revelations received by the Prophet Muhammad transformed this mountain into a symbol of enlightenment for the entire Muslim world.

### Highlights of Hira Makkah History:

- The First Revelation: In 610 CE, the Prophet Muhammad was sent the first verses of the Qur’an while meditating in Hira Cave, Makkah.
- Prophet Muhammad’s Retreat: The Prophet spent several years retreating to this cave to reflect, meditate, and seek spiritual guidance.
- Symbol of Spiritual Reflection: To this day, Jabal al Nour remains a symbol of the Prophet’s search for truth and the beginning of the Islamic revelation.

Jabal al Nour’s importance is not just historical but also symbolic. It represents the journey of seeking knowledge, peace, and enlightenment—values that resonate deeply with Muslims worldwide.

## Hira Makkah and the Surrounding Area

While the ascent to Hira Makkah Mountain is vital to a spiritual pilgrimage, the surrounding area is equally rich in attractions. Makkah is a city brimming with Islamic heritage, and there are several vital places every visitor should see.

### Makkah Tourist Attractions :

- The Grand Mosque (Masjid al-Haram): The holiest site in Islam, home to the Kaaba.
- Jannat al-Mu’alla: The sacred cemetery where several family members of the Prophet Muhammad are buried.
- Mount Thawr: Another important mountain in Islamic history, where the Prophet Muhammad hid during his migration to Madinah.

If you’re visiting Makkah, it’s worth exploring some of these Makkah tourist attractions to gain a deeper understanding of the city’s profound history.

For those planning to stay a while, check out the Grand Makkah Hotel , conveniently located near the holy sites. Additionally, there are a variety of other hotels in Makkah suited to different preferences and budgets.

## Living in Makkah: Finding Your Home

Makkah is more than just a pilgrimage destination; it’s also where many choose to live, drawn by the city’s spiritual energy and historical significance. If you’re considering purchasing property in Makkah, there are several key areas to explore:

Whether planning a short stay or considering settling in, Makkah offers a range of real estate options to fit your needs. Visiting Hira Makkah is a journey of spiritual reflection and connection. Whether you’re retracing the steps of the Prophet Muhammad or simply looking to explore the historic wonders of Jabal al Nour , the experience will leave an indelible mark on your soul.

### How long does it take to climb Jabal al Nour?

Climbing Jabal al Nour typically takes 45 minutes to two hours, depending on your pace and fitness level. Proper preparation, including water and proper footwear, is essential.

### Can anyone visit Hira Makkah Cave?

Anyone can visit Hira Cave, although the climb is physically demanding. Many pilgrims choose to make the journey part of their visit to Makkah, but it’s also open to tourists.

Jabal al Nour is one of the most important mountains in Islamic history. It’s where the Prophet Muhammad received the first revelation of the Qur’an, marking the beginning of Islam’s spread worldwide.

The best time to visit Mount Hira is between November and February when the weather is cooler and the mountain is less crowded. Early mornings are also ideal.

In reality, the Edge of the World Riyadh is a breathtaking natural wonder just outside Saudi Arabia’s capital, Riyadh. Also known as Jebel Fihrayn, this striking desert landmark has become a must-see for locals and international tourists. With its stunning panoramic views and sheer cliffs that stretch forever, it’s no wonder the Edge of the World Riyadh tour has captured the imagination of so many.

## What is the Edge of the World?

The Edge of the World, or the End of the World Riyadh, is part of the larger Tuwaiq Escarpment, which runs about 800 kilometers through central Saudi Arabia. The site gets its name from the dramatic views that make visitors feel as if they are standing on the edge of the earth, gazing into an endless desert horizon. The vast, arid plains below the cliffs give the impression of infinity, hence the dramatic name.

While exploring the Edge of World Riyadh, visitors often find themselves surrounded by silence, save for the occasional breeze and perhaps the distant call of a desert bird. The landscape is both awe-inspiring and humbling, reminding visitors of the vastness of nature and the timelessness of the world.

## How to Get to the Edge of the World Riyadh

Reaching this remote site might sound challenging, but it’s accessible from Riyadh. Just about 90 kilometers northwest of the city, the drive to the Edge of the World Riyadh takes roughly 1.5 to 2 hours, depending on the vehicle and road conditions.

- By Car: If you’re feeling adventurous, you can embark on a self-drive trip to the Edge of the World. However, be sure to rent a reliable 4×4 vehicle. The journey’s last 20-30 kilometers consist of unpaved, rocky paths that can be challenging for standard cars.
- Riyadh Edge of the World Tours: For those who prefer to let someone else take care of the logistics, joining a guided tour is a great option. Numerous Edge of the World Riyadh tour companies offer day trips that include transportation, guides, and even refreshments. Some tours offer guided hikes, while others focus on enjoying the sunset over the cliffs.

Whether you go on your own or with a tour, the drive to the world edge Riyadh offers its own charm, taking you through vast desert landscapes, small villages, and rugged terrain. Be sure to stock up on water and snacks, as services are limited along the way.

## What to Do at the Edge of the World Riyadh

Once you arrive at the Edge of World Riyadh, the adventure truly begins. Here are some of the most popular activities:

### 1. Hiking

The Edge of the World Riyadh offers many hiking opportunities for all skill levels. You can take a leisurely walk along the top of the escarpment to enjoy the panoramic views, or for those seeking more of a challenge, steeper trails lead down the cliffs. Hiking along the edge at sunset or sunrise is popular, as the golden light transforms the desert landscape into a breathtaking scene.

### 2. Photography

For photographers, the End of the World Riyadh is a dream. The dramatic cliffs, endless desert horizon, and ever-changing light provide the perfect backdrop for stunning photographs. Whether you’re an amateur with a smartphone or a professional with a high-end camera, you’re bound to capture some unforgettable images.

### 3. Camping

Some Edge of the World Riyadh tour operators offer overnight camping trips, allowing you to experience the serenity of the desert after dark. Stargazing in the Arabian desert is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Away from city lights, the night sky at the Edge of the World is brilliantly clear, with stars filling the sky like diamonds.

### 4. Wildlife Spotting

Despite its arid environment, the World Edge Riyadh is home to various wildlife. You might spot camels, lizards, and desert birds like falcons and eagles. While the wildlife is not abundant, it’s always exciting to encounter animals adapted to such harsh conditions.

### 5. Picnicking

Bring a picnic to enjoy at the Edge of the World if you’re on a day trip. Several flat areas provide ideal spots to sit down, relax, and enjoy a meal while enjoying the spectacular views. Just be sure to take all your rubbish with you, as the area is a protected natural site, and keeping it clean is essential for future visitors.

## Best Time to Visit the Edge of the World Riyadh

Timing is everything when planning a trip to the Edge of the World Riyadh. While the site can be visited year-round, certain seasons and times of day offer a more pleasant experience.

- Season: The best time to visit is during the cooler months, from October to April. In the summer, temperatures can soar well over 40°C, making exploring the area uncomfortable and potentially dangerous. Winter offers more moderate temperatures, which are ideal for hiking and enjoying the outdoors.
- Time of Day: Early morning or late afternoon are the best times to visit, particularly if you want to avoid the rough midday sun. Sunset at the Edge of the World Riyadh is incredibly stunning, as the sun casts a warm glow over the cliffs and desert.

## Why Visit the Edge of the World Riyadh?

There are many reasons why the Edge of the World is a must-see attraction. Here’s why it should be on your bucket list:

- Unique Landscape: The Edge of the World Riyadh is unlike any other place in Saudi Arabia. The dramatic cliffs and expansive views offer an unforgettable experience, whether you’re an avid hiker or simply want to marvel at nature’s beauty.
- Easy Access from Riyadh: Despite its remote appearance, the End of the World Riyadh is just a short drive from the capital city. Its proximity makes it an ideal day trip for those living in or visiting Riyadh.
- A True Adventure: Whether you opt for a self-drive trip or an organized Edge of the World Riyadh tour, getting to the site is an adventure. The journey through the desert and the incredible views at the destination make for a memorable experience.

## Other Attractions Near Riyadh

While the Edge of the World Riyadh is undoubtedly a highlight, there are plenty of other places to visit in Riyadh and the surrounding areas. Whether you’re interested in historical landmarks, cultural sites, or more natural beauty, Riyadh has something to offer every traveler.

Some tourist attractions in Riyadh include:

- Diriyah: The historic town of Diriyah, a UNESCO site, is just a short drive from Riyadh. It was once the seat of power for the Saudi royal family and offers a glimpse into the country’s rich history.
- Al Masmak Fortress: This fortress played a vital role in the forging of modern Saudi Arabia. It’s a fascinating site for anyone interested in the country’s heritage.
- King Abdullah Park: For those who prefer greenery, King Abdullah Park is a beautiful, landscaped park perfect for a stroll.

If you’re planning a longer trip, explore other places to visit in Saudi , such as Al-Ula, the Red Sea coastline, or the mountainous regions in the southwest.

For more information on tourism in Saudi Arabia , check out our guides to the best sightseeing places in Riyadh and beyond. Whether a local or a visitor, the Edge of the World Riyadh is an experience you won’t want to miss.

## FAQs About the Edge of the World Riyadh

### What is the best time to visit the Edge of the World Riyadh?

The best time to visit is during the cooler months, from October to April. Early morning or late afternoon are ideal for avoiding the heat and enjoying the stunning sunset views.

### Can I drive to the Edge of the World Riyadh myself?

Yes, but you’ll need a 4×4 vehicle for the last part of the journey. Alternatively, you can join an organized Edge of the World Riyadh tour.

### Is it safe to visit the Edge of the World?

Yes, it’s generally safe as long as you’re prepared. Bring plenty of water, wear sun protection, and follow designated paths.

### Are there camping facilities at the Edge of the World Riyadh?

No official camping facilities exist, but some tours offer overnight camping experiences. Be sure to bring your own equipment and leave no trace of your visit.

# A Complete Guide to Safa and Marwah: History, Significance, and Experience

If you’re visiting Makkah, one of the essential things to do is explore the Safa and Marwah mountains. These two small hills carry immense historical and religious significance, especially for Muslims performing Hajj or Umrah. However, their relevance goes beyond ritual, offering a deeper understanding of Islamic history and culture.

In this guide, we’ll delve into the history of Safa Marwa, explore their religious importance, and provide helpful information about places to visit in Mecca to make your journey memorable. Whether you want to learn about Safa Marwah or explore attractions in Makkah, this comprehensive guide covers everything.

What Are Safa and Marwah?

Safa and Marwah (or Safa Marwa, sometimes called) are two small hills located within the Masjid al-Haram, the grand mosque in Makkah. These hills are vital to the Sa’i ritual, which is one of the mandatory elements of both the Hajj and Umrah pilgrimages. The Sa’i involves walking seven times between Safa and Marwah, commemorating Hagar’s search for water for her son, Ismail.

The walk between Safa & Marwah holds deep spiritual value, reminding Muslims of Hagar’s unwavering faith in Allah as she searched tirelessly in the desert.

## The History of Safa Marwah: A Journey Through Time

Understanding the history of Safa Marwah is crucial for anyone planning to visit these sacred hills.

- Hagar’s Story: The origin of Marwah Safa dates back to the time of Prophet Ibrahim. When Hagar was left in the desert with her infant son Ismail, she searched for water between Safa and Marwah. Her persistence led to the miracle of Zamzam water, which began to flow near Ismail’s feet.
- Significance in Hajj and Umrah: Since then, the Sa’i has been integrated into Islamic rituals, where pilgrims reenact Hagar’s search. Today, Safa and Marwah are located inside the Grand Mosque of Makkah, allowing millions of visitors to perform this act of devotion annually.
- A Symbol of Faith: Hagar’s journey represents faith, hope, and perseverance, making it one of the most spiritually significant attractions in Makkah.

## How to Experience Safa and Marwah During Your Visit?

Visiting Safa Marwa is a profound experience, especially during pilgrimage seasons. But you don’t have to be on Hajj or Umrah to witness these sacred sites. Here are some things you need to know:

- Location: Safa and Marwah are located inside the Grand Mosque. Since the mosque is one of the largest in the world, there is plenty of space for visitors.
- The Ritual of Sa’i: If you’re performing Sa’i, start at Safa, walk to Marwah, and return—completing this journey seven times. The total distance is about 3.15 kilometers, which might take some time but offers a spiritual connection.
- Best Time to Visit: Pilgrims usually perform Sa’i during their Hajj or Umrah. However, non-pilgrims can visit Safa and Marwah during less crowded times, outside significant pilgrimage seasons.

## Key Attractions in Makkah Near Safa and Marwah

While Safa & Marwah are central to any pilgrimage, Makkah offers much more than religious rituals. Whether you’re a history enthusiast or seeking a complete spiritual experience, Makkah has several vital attractions worth exploring.

- Masjid al-Haram (The Grand Mosque): As the largest mosque in the world, it encompasses both Safa and Marwah. Make time to explore its intricate architecture and the spiritual energy that permeates this holy site.
- The Kaaba: Located within the Grand Mosque, the Kaaba is the main point of prayer for Muslims worldwide. During Hajj or Umrah, pilgrims circle the Kaaba seven times as part of their worship.
- Abraj Al-Bait Clock Tower: Just steps away from the Grand Mosque, this towering structure is one of the tallest buildings in the world. It houses a luxury hotel, shopping center, and museum. Visitors can enjoy a panoramic view of Makkah from the observation deck.
- Zamzam Well: Don’t miss visiting the Zamzam Well near the Kaaba. This miraculous water source is linked to the history of Safa Marwah, and pilgrims often drink from it, believing in its purifying and healing properties.

## Other Must-Visit Places to Explore in Makkah

In addition to the sacred sites, places to visit in Mecca offer a mix of historical, cultural, and modern experiences. Here are a few noteworthy spots:

- Mount Arafat: This is the location where the Prophet Muhammad Peace Be Upin Him delivered his final sermon during the Hajj. It is highly recommended for its historical and religious significance.
- Jabal Al-Nou r: Known as the “Mountain of Light,” this site is where Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) received his first revelation. Hiking up the mountain offers a glimpse into the early days of Islam.
- Al Diyafa Mall: This shopping center offers modern conveniences, from clothing to dining.

## Things to Do in Makkah: Beyond Religious Pilgrimage

While Makkah is primarily known for its religious significance, you can engage in a variety of activities that will enrich your trip.

- Shopping: From traditional souks to modern malls, shopping is a popular pastime in Makkah. Local handicrafts, perfumes, prayer mats, and other religious items will be found.

Safa and Marwah represent Hagar’s faith and perseverance in searching for water for her son Ismail. Today, Muslims reenact her journey during the Sa’i, a key ritual in both Hajj and Umrah.

The walk between Safa and Marwah is about 3.15 kilometers, as pilgrims must walk between the two hills seven times. Each round trip covers approximately 450 meters.

Yes, non-pilgrims can visit Safa and Marwah outside the Hajj season, although the area is most commonly visited during Hajj and Umrah.

# Jabal Al Nour: An Amazing Journey Through Makkah’s Spiritual Landmark

If you’re planning a visit to Makkah, especially during Umrah, you’ll find that there’s so much more to it than the iconic sites of Masjid Al Haram and the Kaaba. Among the places to visit in Makkah, Jabal Al Nour stands out not just for its history but also for the deeply spiritual significance it holds in Islamic tradition.

## What Is Jabal Al Nour?

Jabal Al Nour, translated as the “Mountain of Light,” is located approximately three kilometers northeast of the Grand Mosque in Makkah. This mountainous peak is celebrated in Islamic history as the site where Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) got his first revelation from the Angel Gabriel in the Hira Cave.

For those interested in visiting Jabal Al Nour Makkah, the trek to this sacred site is a spiritual journey. The climb up Jabal Nour can be demanding, but it’s worth every step for many pilgrims and tourists. The view from the summit provides an awe-inspiring panorama of Makkah and its surrounding landscape, adding to the depth of this spiritual experience.

## Why You Should Visit Jabal Al Nour

1. Historical Significance: Jabal Al Nour is not just a natural wonder. It’s a place with profound religious importance. Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) frequently visited the Cave of Hira at the top of the mountain for reflection and meditation before the revelation.
2. Cave of Hira: The focal point of Jabal Nour is the Cave of Hira, where the first verses of the Quran are revealed. This small cave can only accommodate a few people at a time, making it a place of quiet reflection.
3. Spiritual Journey: Climbing Jabal Al Nour isn’t just a physical challenge; it’s an emotional and spiritual one, too. As you ascend the mountain, the effort becomes a metaphor for spiritual growth and seeking divine guidance.
4. Breathtaking Views: Once at the top, you’ll have a magnificent view of Makkah. The quietness of the summit is a stark contrast to the bustling city below, providing an opportunity for meditation and contemplation.

## Climbing Jabal Al Nour: What to Expect

- Duration: The climb typically takes 1.5 to 2 hours, depending on your pace and level of fitness. It is steep and can be strenuous, so be prepared.
- Footwear: Good hiking shoes are essential, as the path is rocky and uneven.
- Water: Bring plenty of water. There are no facilities along the trail, and Makkah’s heat can be overwhelming.
- Best Time to Visit: Early morning is the ideal time to start your climb to avoid the midday heat. Alternatively, the late afternoon also offers a chance to catch a breathtaking sunset over Makkah.

## Other Places to Visit in Makkah During Umrah

Makkah is full of spiritually significant and culturally rich sites. Here are some places to visit in Makkah during Umrah that will enhance your pilgrimage experience:

- King Khalid Grand Mosque : A significant mosque in the heart of Makkah.
- Walyal Ahd District : A fascinating district with historical roots.
- Grand Makkah Hotel : One of the luxurious places to stay near Jabal Al Nour. It offers proximity to important religious landmarks.
- Makkah Tourist Attraction s: Explore the broader attractions of Makkah beyond the pilgrimage sites and tourism in Saudi Arabia .

## Practical Tips for Visiting Jabal Al Nour Mecca

- Dress Modestly: Always remember you’re visiting a religious site, so appropriate attire is necessary. Both men and women should wear modest clothing.
- Be Mindful of Crowds: Although the climb to Jabal Nour isn’t as crowded as Masjid Al Haram, the cave at the summit can get busy during peak seasons.
- Hire a Guide: If you need clarification on the climb or want to learn more about the site’s history, you can hire a guide. Some locals offer guided tours to help explain the mountain’s significance and place in Islamic history.

## Jabal Al Nour in Makkah’s Broader Religious Landscape

Makkah is home to numerous religious and historical sites. While Jabal Al Nour holds its own unique place, many other places to visit in Mecca add to the spiritual depth of your journey. Here are a few:

- Mount Arafat: Another highly significant Islamic site where Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) delivered his final sermon during Hajj.
- Mina: Famous for the annual Hajj pilgrimage, Mina is where pilgrims perform the symbolic devil stoning.
- Masjid Al Haram: Of course, no visit to Makkah is complete without spending time at the Grand Mosque, home to the Kaaba, the most sacred site in Islam.

These sites offer rich Islamic history and are deeply embedded in the religious practices of Muslims worldwide.

## Where to Stay Near Jabal Al Nour

Given that Jabal Al Nour is situated in Makkah, there are plenty of accommodation options nearby, making your visit more convenient.

- Grand Makkah Hotel: A luxurious stay with proximity to many religious landmarks, including Jabal Nour.
- Walyal Ahd District: If you’re looking to explore Makkah beyond its religious sites, this district offers insight into the local culture and daily life.

Beyond its religious significance, Makkah is a thriving city with real estate opportunities for those interested in investing. If you’re considering settling in Makkah or investing in property, check out these options:

- Apartments for sale in An Nuzhah

- Apartments for sale in Ash Sharai
- Apartments for sale in Batha Quraysh

These areas are great for long-term investment and offer an opportunity to immerse yourself in Makkah’s rich culture and heritage.

## FAQs About Jabal Al Nour

Here are some commonly asked questions about Jabal Al Nour Mecca to help you better understand the site and plan your visit.

### How long does it take to climb Jabal Al Nour?

The climb typically takes 1.5 to 2 hours, depending on your pace and level of fitness. It’s a strenuous climb, so it’s important to be prepared.

### Is Jabal Al Nour open to visitors year-round?

Yes, Jabal Al Nour is accessible throughout the year, but it is best to visit during the cooler months or early in the morning to avoid the heat.

### Can I visit Jabal Al Nour during Umrah?

Absolutely. Many pilgrims include a visit to Jabal Nour as part of their spiritual journey during Umrah. It’s one of the places to visit in Makkah during Umrah.

### What is the significance of the Cave of Hira?

The Cave of Hira, located at the summit of Jabal Al Nour, is where Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) received the first revelation from the Angel Gabriel. It’s one of the most sacred places in Islamic history.

# Al Balad Jeddah: The Heart of the Stunning Jeddah Historic District

Al Balad Jeddah is more than just an area in the city; it’s a journey into the past, a walk through the winding streets where history meets the present. Nestled in the vibrant landscape of Jeddah, Al Balad is a must-visit for anyone eager to explore the depths of Saudi Arabia’s rich cultural heritage.

## The Charm of Jeddah Districts

Jeddah is a city of contrasts, where modernity coexists with tradition. Its districts each tell a unique story, from the upscale vibes of Tahlia Street Jeddah to the tranquil residential zones like Faisaliyah Jeddah District . But among all the Jeddah districts, Al Balad stands out for its historical significance.

Al Balad, or “The Town,” is the historic center of Jeddah and one of the most well-preserved districts in Saudi Arabia. Walking through its narrow alleys, you’ll be transported back to the days when Jeddah was the gateway to Mecca, bustling with traders and pilgrims from across the globe.

## A Glimpse into Al Balad Jeddah’s History

Al Balad was founded in the 7th century, serving as the commercial hub for merchants traveling to the Arabian Peninsula. The area flourished, becoming a significant trade center, especially during the Ottoman period. Today, Al Balad Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, retains much of its old-world charm, with coral-stone houses, ancient mosques, and vibrant markets that give visitors a taste of what life was like centuries ago.

One of the most remarkable features of Al Balad is its architecture. The traditional houses, built from coral and reinforced with wood, are iconic. Many of these homes are adorned with rawasheen—intricate wooden lattice windows that offer privacy and ventilation, a practical design element in the hot desert climate.

## Exploring the Jeddah Old Town: What to See

When you step into Jeddah Old Town, you enter a world where every corner is of importance. Here are some of the must-see landmarks:

- Naseef House: One of the most famous buildings in Al Balad, Naseef House was once the home of a wealthy merchant family. Now a museum, it provides deep knowledge into the traditional lifestyle of Jeddah’s residents.
- Al Shafi’i Mosque: This is one of the oldest mosques in Jeddah, dating back to the 13th century.
- Bab Makkah: One of the original gates to the old city, Bab Makkah, served as the entrance for pilgrims heading to Mecca. Today, it stands as a reminder of the city’s religious significance.
- Al Balad Market: No visit to Al Balad is complete without wandering through its bustling markets, which offer everything from traditional spices to handcrafted souvenirs.

## Al Balad Jeddah Shopping Experience

Shopping in Al Balad Jeddah is an experience unlike any other. The vibrant souks are filled with sights, sounds, and smells of a bygone era. Whether you’re looking for traditional Saudi clothing, intricate jewelry, or unique handicrafts, Al Balad’s markets have something for everyone.

- Balad Market Jeddah: This is the heart of shopping in Al Balad. Here, you can find various goods, from antiques to textiles. The market is also famous for its spices, with vendors offering everything from saffron to cardamom.
- Souq Al Alawi: One of the largest markets in Al Balad, Souq Al Alawi is a labyrinth of narrow streets with shops selling a variety of goods. Here, you can haggle with vendors and discover hidden gems.
- Gold Souq: Located in the heart of Al Balad, the Gold Souq is where you can find exquisite jewelry crafted by skilled artisans. The intricate designs reflect the region’s rich cultural heritage.

## The Role of Al Balad in Jeddah Historic District

Al Balad is not just a district; it’s a living museum, a testament to Jeddah’s rich history. The area is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, a status that underscores its importance in Saudi Arabia’s cultural and historical fabric.

The preservation of Al Balad is a priority for the Saudi government, which has undertaken various initiatives to restore and maintain the historic buildings. The district’s unique architecture, with its coral stone structures and wooden balconies, reflects the city’s past and symbolizes its enduring legacy.

Al Balad’s role in the Jeddah Historic District is also crucial for tourism. The area attracts visitors from all over the world, eager to explore its narrow streets, visit its historic landmarks, and experience the vibrant culture that has flourished here for centuries.

## Al Balad Jeddah Shopping: A Blend of Old and New

While Al Balad is steeped in history, it’s also a place where tradition meets modernity. The shopping experience in Al Balad, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, perfectly exemplifies this blend. In addition to the traditional souks, there are modern shops and boutiques where you can find contemporary fashion, electronics, and other goods.

- Traditional Souks: As mentioned earlier, the traditional markets are a highlight of any visit to Al Balad. These souks offer a glimpse into the past, where you can buy items made using methods passed down through generations.
- Modern Boutiques: In recent years, Al Balad Jeddah has seen the rise of modern boutiques and shops that cater to the tastes of today’s shoppers. These stores offer everything from fashion to technology, contrasting the traditional markets.
- Al Balad Market Jeddah: This market is a prime example of how Al Balad has evolved. While it retains its traditional charm, the market has also embraced modernity, with shops offering a mix of old and new products.

## Living in Al Balad Jeddah: A Unique Experience

Living in Al Balad is like stepping into a different world. The area is not just a tourist destination; it’s a vibrant community where people live, work, and raise families. The homes in Al Balad Jeddah are a mix of traditional and modern architecture, reflecting the district’s unique character.

- Traditional Homes: The traditional homes in Al Balad Jeddah are made of coral stone and wood, with intricate wooden balconies that offer stunning views of the surrounding area. These homes are a testament to the craftsmanship of the past, each telling a story of the people who lived there.
- Modern Living: While Al Balad is steeped in history, it has also embraced modernity. Many of the area’s homes have been renovated to include modern amenities, making them comfortable and convenient for today’s residents.
- Community Life: Living in Al Balad means being part of a close-knit community where neighbors know each other and have a strong sense of belonging. The area is also home to various cultural events and festivals, which bring the community together and celebrate the district’s rich heritage.

## Real Estate in Jeddah: Finding Your Home in Historic and Modern Districts

While Al Balad offers a unique living experience steeped in history, other Jeddah districts provide diverse real estate options for those who want to settle in this vibrant city. Whether you’re interested in historic homes or modern apartments, there’s something for everyone.

- Properties for Sale in Al Marwah : Al Marwah is known for its affordable housing options, making it an excellent choice for first-time homebuyers. The district offers a mix of apartments and villas catering to various budgets.
- Properties for Sale in Ar Rawdah : Ar Rawdah is a prestigious district in Jeddah, known for its luxurious homes and upscale amenities. The area is home to some of the city’s best schools, restaurants, and shopping centers.

Al Balad Jeddah is known for its rich history, traditional architecture, and vibrant markets. It’s a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a must-visit destination for anyone interested in exploring Saudi Arabia’s cultural heritage.

Al Balad Jeddah is centrally located in Jeddah and is easy to access by car, taxi, or public transportation. If you’re staying at one of the Jeddah hotels , you can take a taxi to the historic district. The area is well-signposted, but once you’re there, it’s best explored on foot to truly appreciate its charm.

### What can I buy at Al Balad Market Jeddah?

At Al Balad Market, you can find many products, from traditional Saudi clothing and jewelry to spices and handcrafted souvenirs. The market is also famous for its antique shops, where you can find unique items that reflect the region’s cultural heritage.

### Is Al Balad Jeddah an excellent place to visit for tourists?

Absolutely! Al Balad Jeddah is one of the top tourist attractions in the city. Its history, culture, and shopping blend make it a unique visitor experience. Whether you are interested in architecture and history or simply exploring the local markets, Al Balad has something to offer everyone.
